summary: CWE-760: the bad() entry point derived the hash salt from java.util.Random, whose output is predictable because it is seeded from the clock and uses a non-cryptographic PRNG. I switched the salt source to java.security.SecureRandom (already imported) and generate the salt from raw random bytes via nextBytes, producing an unpredictable salt. The feature (salting the SHA-512 digest of "hash me" and writing the hex) is preserved; valid behavior still runs.
